content:
Cabinet considered a report of the Chief
Executive providing an update on correspondence with the Secretary
of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government since the
decision in respect of Local Government Reorganisation in
Hampshire. The report sought a delegation to challenge the
Secretary of State’s decision, should external legal advice
indicate the County Council had an arguable case.
 
The Chairman noted that this decision was not
a final decision regarding launching a legal challenge as it was
subject to further legal advice. It was agreed that all group
leaders would be kept informed of developments.
 
The Chairman indicated that the reason for
taking this course of action was concern for the future
sustainability of local government services. It was considered that
the Government had not provided sufficient justification for the
choice of which Local Government Reorganisation proposal to pursue,
and that for a decision of such significance such justification
should be provided. This was not intended to be a rejection of the
need for local government reform, rather a preference that the way
forward be reached by consensus based on an agreed economic model.
It was considered to be in the public interest to challenge the
decision, in order to ensure public services are sustainable in the
future.
 
The recommendations in the report were
considered and agreed unanimously by Cabinet Members in attendance.
A Decision Record is attached to these minutes.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to challenge the Secretary of State's decision on Local Government Reorganisation in Hampshire.

content:
Cabinet considered a report of the Director of
Universal Services presenting Hampshire County Council’s
first statutory Biodiversity Report, prepared in accordance with
the Environment Act 2021. The report set out how the Council had
met its biodiversity duty between January 2023 and December 2025
and sought approval for its publication.
 
Members noted that the report had been
developed collaboratively across the organisation and with
partners, and was structured around key thematic areas
demonstrating how biodiversity considerations were embedded across
Council functions. Case studies were highlighted illustrating the
practical impact of the Council’s work, including habitat
creation linked to infrastructure schemes, the delivery of mini
forest projects through the Hampshire Forest Partnership, species
recovery initiatives, and opportunities for residents to benefit
from access to nature.
 
Cabinet welcomed the positive feedback from
the Universal Services Select Committee and noted the intention to
publish a more accessible summary alongside the full report. The
relationship between the Biodiversity Report and the Local Nature
Recovery Strategy was clarified, with the latter identified as the
framework guiding future activity and investment.
 
Members discussed partnerships, engagement
with communities, the role of biodiversity net gain in development,
and opportunities to share learning and best practice across
authorities. The importance of continued leadership and partnership
working to protect Hampshire’s natural environment alongside
development pressures was emphasised.
 
The recommendations in the report were
considered and agreed. A Decision Record is attached to these
minutes.

content:
Cabinet considered a report of the Director of
Adults’ Health and Care providing an update on the future of
HCC Care residential and nursing homes and the associated Older
Adults’ wider residential and nursing home strategy following
the decision by Cabinet to halt the Care Home Improvement
Programme?on 21 March 2025.??
 
It was noted that 12 CQC?registered homes
would be operated, providing 827 beds across residential, nursing,
short?term and respite care, with 92% of homes rated Good, and
occupancy increasing from 86% towards a 95% target, with recent
occupancy over 90%.  Since March 2025,
improvements in market conditions following the introduction of the
care home framework had stabilised prices and ensured sufficient
supply.  In this context, the business
case for the earlier capital improvement programme (CHIP) was now
unsound given higher capital costs and better value via the market.
 Targeted investment had reopened 88
beds following refurbishments at four homes, with a further
£1.66m planned for safety, accessibility and environment
improvements.
 
The recommendations in the report were
considered and agreed. A Decision Record is attached to these
minutes.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve recommendations regarding the future of HCC Care residential and nursing homes.

content:
Cabinet considered a report of the Director of
Public Health regarding a proposal to provide a seat on the Health
and Wellbeing Board for additional organisations.
 
Cabinet endorsed proposals to strengthen the
Health and Wellbeing Board’s membership to enhance system
collaboration and evidence?led practice.
During the discussion it was noted that due to
changes to Integrated Care Boards (ICBs), the Frimley ICB would
cease to exist at the end of March 2026, therefore it was proposed,
and agreed, the membership of the Health and Wellbeing Board be
updated to also to reflect that change.
 
The recommendations in the report were
considered and agreed, subject to the addition of a recommendation
to cease membership of the Frimley ICB with effect from 1 April
2026.  A Decision Record is attached to
these minutes.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to strengthen the Health and Wellbeing Board's membership by adding additional organisations and updating it to reflect changes in Integrated Care Boards.

content:
Cabinet considered a report of the Director of
Public Health providing an update on the County Council’s
statutory responsibilities for community safety and to outline the
activities undertaken to fulfil duties. 
It was noted that the County Council’s role complemented the
statutory duties of district and borough community safety
partnerships, and that collaboration varied across areas with work
focused on identified need.
 
The recommendations in the report were
considered and agreed. A Decision Record is attached to these
minutes.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve recommendations for the County Council's statutory responsibilities for community safety.

content:
Cabinet considered the Annual Report of the
Director of Public Health 2025 on Let’s Call Time on Alcohol
Harm.  The wide?ranging impacts of
alcohol on health, families and communities were noted, together
with progress achieved locally and the need to intensify
prevention, early intervention and visibility of treatment
services.  Members discussed patterns of
social and binge drinking, inequalities, and the role of licensing
partners, noting ongoing work to support professionals to have
earlier conversations and to reduce stigma as a barrier to
accessing support.
 
The recommendations in the report were
considered and agreed. A Decision Record is attached to these
minutes.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve recommendations in the Annual Report on Let's Call Time on Alcohol Harm.

content:
Cabinet considered a report of the Chief
Financial Officer and Director of Corporate Operations providing
the view of the Chief Financial Officer as to the robustness of the
estimates included in the budget and the adequacy of the financial
reserves.
 
The Chief Financial Officer presented the
report, confirming that estimates were robust. It was noted that at
a 4.99% council tax increase, reserves were assessed as
‘adequate with risk’ for 2026/27 but ‘not
adequate’ for 2027/28; at 14.99%, reserves were
‘adequate’ for 2026/27 and ‘adequate with
risk’ for 2027/28. During discussion, comments of the
External auditors recognising strong financial management and an
unqualified value?for?money conclusion were emphasised.
 
The recommendations in the report were
considered and agreed. A Decision Record is attached to these
minutes.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve recommendations on financial reserves and council tax increase for the upcoming years.

content:
Cabinet considered a report of the Director of
Corporate Operations providing an update on the County
Council’s financial position for 2025/26 as at end of
November 2025.
 
A forecast underspend of £37.8m against
the 2025/26 revenue budget was noted. 
However, it was emphasised that the budget remained balanced
in?year by a planned draw from reserves, reduced from £64.9m
to £27.2m.  Directorate positions
were noted, including pressures in Adults’ Services and
improvements in Children’s Services, particularly due to
slowing demand and activity in Home to School Transport.
 Delivery of £95m in?year SP25
savings was reported, with SP25 remaining on track to over?deliver
by £2.1m by 2027/28.  The position
on the capital programme, with a forecast £278m, and treasury
management was noted.  The significant
DSG deficit position, forecast at £354m, was highlighted for
consideration alongside the budget report.
 
The recommendations in the report were
considered and agreed. A Decision Record is attached to these
minutes.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve recommendations regarding the County Council's financial position for 2025/26.

purpose:

Hampshire 2050 seeking approval to adopt and publish the Hampshire
Skills Strategy.
content:
Cabinet considered a report of the Director of
Hampshire 2050 seeking approval to adopt and publish the Hampshire
Skills Strategy. The strategy was developed in response to changes
in the skills landscape, including the dissolution of Local
Enterprise Partnerships and new funding arrangements. The new
Strategy covered the area that was due to become a Mayoral Combined
County Authority (MCCA) to support the development of a skills
commissioning strategy, which was due to be an early task for the
MCCA.
 
Members discussed the importance of business
engagement, lifelong learning, and the challenges posed by
employment costs and skills shortages. The strategy’s six
priorities were endorsed, including aligning training with economic
need, removing participation barriers, strengthening careers
guidance, supporting digital and green skills, deepening
employer-provider collaboration, and enabling upskilling for the
adult workforce.
 
The recommendations in the report were
considered and agreed. A Decision Record is attached to these
minutes.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the adoption and publication of the Hampshire Skills Strategy to address changes in the skills landscape.

content:
Cabinet considered an annual report from the
Director of Adults’ Health and Care on delivery of the
Prevent duty, noting the substantial terrorism threat level and the
impact of global conflicts on local risks. The report confirmed
robust compliance with Home Office requirements, strong governance,
and effective partnership working. Achievements included high staff
training uptake, enhanced school engagement, and strengthened
leadership. Members welcomed the positive assurance received from
the Home Office and the ongoing evolution of processes to address
radicalisation and extremism.
 
The recommendations in the report were
considered and agreed. A Decision Record is attached to these
minutes.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve recommendations in an annual report on addressing radicalisation and extremism.

content:

Director of Adults’ Health and Care, which provided assurance
regarding safeguarding arrangements and the quality of social care
provision. Despite a significant rise in safeguarding referrals,
the directorate demonstrated strong performance through improved
practice, training, and digital tools to support data driven
decision making. The importance of voluntary sector involvement and
multi-agency partnership working was emphasised, and Members
welcomed the ongoing commitment to continuous improvement and
learning.
 
The recommendations in the report were
considered and agreed. A Decision Record is attached to these
minutes.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve recommendations for the quality of social care provision and safeguarding arrangements in the Director of Adults' Health and Care

content:

Director of Children’s Services, which highlighted strong
performance in safeguarding, including a 15% reduction in children
subject to child protection plans (compared to a national increase)
and improved timeliness of assessments. ‘Family help’
teams had been rolled out early. The report noted ongoing
challenges such as increased demand and the complexity of cases, as
well as the importance of robust multi-agency working and workforce
sufficiency.
 
Members commended the outstanding rating
achieved by the service following an inspection earlier in the year
and the effectiveness of early intervention and partnership
working.
 
The recommendations in the report were
considered and agreed. A Decision Record is attached to these
minutes.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve recommendations from the Director of Children's Services annual report, highlighting strong performance in safeguarding and ongoing challenges.

content:
Cabinet considered a report of the Director of
Universal Services regarding the proposed medium?term business plan
for the six Outdoor and Study Centres, which outlined strong
performance, increased usage, and essential maintenance
requirements totalling just under £2 million over three
years. The plan aimed to ensure the centres remain safe,
operational, and sustainable through to 2028.
 
The Chairman invited non
executive Members to speak on this topic following requests.
Councillor House expressed concern that the proposed direction of
travel would lead to the closure of the Calshot activities centre
which included rare assets in the velodrome and dry ski slope.
 
Councillor Hayre expressed gratitude that the
Stubbington Centre had been saved from closure by a previous
Cabinet decision and supported the proposal to invest in the
maintenance needs of the centres and consider a sustainable
future.
 
It was noted that the proposed Business Plan
had been considered by the Universal Services Select Committee the
previous day and a letter had been provided to Cabinet and added to
the papers for the meeting reflecting the Committee’s support
for the recommendations to Cabinet.
 
Cabinet Members expressed support for the
centres’ educational and community value and welcomed
bringing together the outdoor and study centres. Concerns regarding
Calshot’s coastal risks were addressed, and assurances were
given that the direction of travel was to sustain and adapt
services rather than closure.
 
The recommendations in the report were
considered and agreed. A Decision Record is attached to these
minutes.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve a medium-term business plan for six Outdoor and Study Centres, despite concerns raised about the potential closure of the Calshot activities centre.

content:
Cabinet considered a report of the Director of
Hampshire 2050 regarding the proposed Local Nature Recovery
Strategy for Hampshire, prepared under the Environment Act 2021
following extensive stakeholder engagement and consultation. The
strategy set out measures to reverse nature’s decline and
would be published following notification to the Secretary of
State, if approved.
 
The impact of increased housing targets on
nature recovery was discussed, and it was agreed that the strategy
would serve as a vital planning tool to guide biodiversity net gain
and protect Hampshire’s natural environment.
 
The recommendations in the report were
considered and agreed. A Decision Record is attached to these
minutes.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the Local Nature Recovery Strategy for Hampshire, aiming to reverse nature's decline and guide biodiversity net gain.

content:
Cabinet received a report from the Director of
Public Health providing an annual update on the Public Health
Strategy, which reported progress against three key themes; healthy
places, healthy lives, and healthy people. The update highlighted
partnership working, systems approaches to obesity, smoking
cessation, and vaccination uptake.
 
Members praised the collaborative nature of
the strategy and the positive outcomes achieved, particularly in
reducing smoking prevalence and promoting healthy environments. The
importance of neighbourhood working and engaging with diverse
communities was discussed, and the ongoing delivery approach was
endorsed.
 
The recommendations in the report were
considered and agreed. A Decision Record is attached to these
minutes.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve recommendations in the annual update on the Public Health Strategy.

content:
Cabinet received a report from the Director of
Adults’ Health and Care providing an update on the progress
made by Adults’ Health and Care to deliver its Vision and
five-year Strategic Plan during 2024/25. The Year Two progress
update noted continued focus on prevention, independent living, and
accommodation and long?term care. Highlights included
technology?enabled care, Meals on Wheels and welfare checks,
expanded carer support, and strong market oversight.
 
The discussion recognised the challenges posed
by demographic changes and increasing complexity of need, as well
as the importance of innovation and partnership working. Members
commended the directorate for its achievements, particularly in
maintaining high standards of care and embracing technology to
support independence.
 
The recommendations in the report were
considered and agreed. A Decision Record is attached to these
minutes.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve recommendations for the progress of Adults' Health and Care in delivering its Vision and five-year Strategic Plan during 2024/25

content:
Cabinet received a report from the Director of
People and Organisation providing details of the Annual Complaints
Report as required by the Local Government Complaints Code, and
including the Local Government and Social Care Ombudsman (LGSCO)
determinations for 2024/25.
 
It was noted that in 2024/25 the complaints
process had been changed to reduce the stages from three to two and
this was the first year of reporting against this new approach.
Numbers of complaints had gone up, however the number proceeding to
stage two had gone down, indicating improvements in resolving
complaints at stage 1. It was also noted that comparative data
showed Hampshire had fewer LGSCO complaints upheld per head of

highlighted.

considered and agreed. A Decision Record is attached to these
minutes.
